text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Kenya's Harambee Stars land 1-0 victory over Guinea in World Cup qualifier.
- Professor Hilary Ojiambo, a pioneer heart surgeon, has died.
- President Daniel arap Moi's declaration that the Rift Valley province is a sealed electoral zone draws angry reactions from Kenyan leaders.
- Ruling party polls in Kiambu district to be held again on Wednesday.
- Bandits invade a residential estate in Isiolo town, eastern Kenya, and kill one woman.
- Opposition leader Michael Kijana Wamalwa says Kenyans should be allowed to carry guns for personal security.
- Stephen Omondi, chairman of Kenya's youngest political opposition party the National Development Party of Kenya, is caught up in a leadership wrangle with Raila Odinga.
- Professor Onesmus Mutungi, chairman of the government appointed Standing Committee on human rights is says he is determined to educate Kenyans on their rights.
- An agreement seeking to end double taxation affecting regional workers in the three East African countries will be signed on Monday in Arusha, Tanzania.

- Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni's ambition to develop an industrial powerhouse away from the politically sensitive Ugandan capital city of Kampala could soon be taking shape at Nakasongola, 100 km (60 miles) northwest of the capital. ($1=54 Kenya Shillings)
